pattern.crimePattern: a near-blind master engraver kills his partner of thirty years in a blackout, in the workshop he can walk without light, to stop him taking their book of forged-seal orders to the prosecutor
pattern.notes: Fictional shop and engravers on a real street of engravers. Closes t_stamp: the first forged REGISTRAR OF TITLES seal was cut twelve years ago "for 4th Floor, Lands House — Records". Hamisi is the son of Rashid, case 10's victim; Juma was Rashid's apprentice.

ob.text: A neighbour reports an engraver found dead in the back room of a seals-and-stamps shop on Kirinyaga Road after a power cut: Jeremiah Owino (64), co-founder of Owino & Mwakazi Seals.

facts.text: Jeremiah Owino was found dead in the back room of Owino & Mwakazi Seals on Thursday evening after a power cut. No door or window was forced.
One heavy blow to the head. His phone on the floor, its torch still on; his bag open and empty.
The till is untouched: KSh 6,300. The brass stock is all there.
The cast-iron hand embosser hangs on its peg wiped and upside down, handle up: the only tool on the wall hung that way.
The shop's paraffin lamp is cold, its wick dry; Daudi's room has no torch; no other phone light was used.
The shop's day book holds thirty years of ordinary orders, and no "Lands" order anywhere.
Pamela: at lunch Jeremiah said, "Tomorrow I'll sleep well for the first time in twelve years." He said Daudi would understand.
Pamela was at home in Umoja all evening.
Pamela: the landlady, Mama Zainabu, was fighting them over the rent.
Kassim: Owino's front stayed dark except a small light at the back, Jeremiah's phone. Nobody came in or out of the front; he'd have seen any light moving.
Kassim: when the power went every shop lit a torch or a lamp. "Everyone does."
Kassim: at 18:30 a young man shouted at Jeremiah, "You made the seal my father refused to make!", then walked off towards the stage.
Kassim was at his own counter with a lamp, in view of three customers.
Kenya Power: the block was off from 19:40 to 20:25.
Records: at 19:20 Jeremiah called the ODPP for 6 minutes; the duty clerk noted he'd bring "a book of orders" at 9 a.m. about forged seals, and asked for Prosecutor Abdi.
The conductor: Hamisi took the 18:50 matatu to Eastleigh; his uncle had him home by 19:30.
Juma's mother and the job board: he signed off at 19:30, was at the stage at 19:35 and at his evening class until 21:30.
Zainabu's daughter: she was home in South C all evening.
Inside Daudi's mattress: a hard-backed black book.
Daudi's cardigan has a blood spot on the right cuff.
The black book's first entry, twelve years ago: "REGISTRAR OF TITLES, round, brass. For: 4th Floor, Lands House — Records. Collected by driver."
An entry after case 10: "Finish Rashid's seal from his proof": the proof taken from Rashid's "Mvua — Friday" drawer.
Later entries: the oval "MV" seal, commissioner stamps, a co-op stamp; payments by Till 880 214.
Fingerprints taken from Daudi in detention.
Post-mortem: one blow from a heavy cast-iron object with a rounded jaw, matching the embosser.
Post-mortem: death on Thursday between 19:40 and 20:25.
Lab: Jeremiah's blood on Daudi's cardigan cuff and in the embosser's jaw hinge.
Lab: a partial print in the embosser's hinge is Daudi's. He uses it daily; the hang and the blood are what matter.
Missing: no torch, lamp or phone light was used by the killer in a forty-five-minute blackout.
Missing: there's no black book in Jeremiah's bag.
Missing: nobody came in or out of the front.
Missing: there's no forced entry.
Missing: there's no record of the old Lands order in the shop's day book.

reconstruction.text: Twelve years ago a "client from Lands" asks Owino & Mwakazi to cut a round REGISTRAR OF TITLES seal; Daudi, the better engraver, does it. Each new order, later paid through Till 880 214, goes into a black book in Daudi's room.

After the papers report Kiprop's murder and Halima's release, Jeremiah decides to go to the prosecutor first. At 19:20 he arranges to bring "a book" in the morning. At 19:30 he tells Daudi. Daudi says nothing.

At 19:40 the block's power goes. Daudi walks the twelve steps he has known for thirty years, takes the cast-iron embosser from its peg, and strikes Jeremiah, who is packing the book by the light of his phone.
He takes the book back to his mattress, hangs the embosser on its peg by touch, upside down, and lies down. At 20:25 the power returns and Kassim comes in to borrow a ladder.

afterVerdict.beat: The black book's first entry, "For: 4th Floor, Lands House — Records", is pinned to the Pattern File.

files.text: Traced to source: the first forged REGISTRAR OF TITLES seal, cut twelve years ago "for 4th Floor, Lands House — Records".

afterVerdict.beat: Hamisi sits at the back of the court at Daudi's plea hearing. Afterwards he asks Amani if he can have his father's half-finished seal proof when the case is closed. Halima says yes.
Amani's notebook: "Records, 4th floor. Mwalimu said a desk on the Lands side. Now the brass says which desk."

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Jeremiah's line and a warrant on Daudi's room. Detain Daudi after the search; prints (6 h) and the blood trace (12 h) come back inside 24 h.
